_about: The fortress rows (the design director's 05:38Z, 06:12Z, 06:15Z and 06:17Z of 22 November 2026; the historian's historian/fortress-garrisons-by-line.md and its addendum). The crews of the fortified lines, by the record's dates, at every stop of the dial, under their switch (stage.json 'fortRows', TC_FORTS); off, none of this is read. A row: [turn, nation, name, province, worth, options]. Worth is divisions times strength; a row of up to one division's worth is one division at that strength, a bigger one two divisions at half it, and it is never filled past its own size. Each is a fortress row of its owner's quality: it takes no place among the five a province holds, no staff ever moves it, and it ends only by battle, starving, or with its country. It never forms on ground its country has lost. Rows of turn 1 stand on the first day of a 1939 grand campaign; later rows come in their own month.
_options: 'out': the turn the record's own orders took it out of its works (ORDERED OUT); at stops 1-2 it leaves then, with its men to the reserve, and at stops 3-5 it stays until beaten. 'joins': a row that grows the named fortress row of its nation by its worth (the Guardia alla Frontiera from June 1940); with that row gone it forms on its own. 'mark': 'judgment' where the rules builder split a line's worth between provinces of the chart (checked by the historian, 06:20Z addendum, and ruled as data 06:17Z), 'unsure' where the historian marks the worth so.

_notes.France: Metz, Lauter and Montmedy are release 1's rows in setup-1939.json and are not repeated. Upper Rhine is Colmar 0.71 + Mulhouse 0.31 + Altkirch 0.23. The Alps' 2.5 is the historian's middle of 2-3; the chart has no Dauphine, so Savoy keeps Briancon's share. The northern sectors stayed as skeleton crews when their armies marched into Belgium. Montherme was broken on 15 May, not ordered out: no 'out'.
_notes.Italy: The Guardia alla Frontiera by threat, not frontier length: at 3.3 (June 1940) Piedmont 1.0, Liguria 0.4, Lombardy 0.25, Alto Adige 0.35, Friuli 1.35 (3.35 as ruled); the 1.4 of the first day is each times 0.42. It went WITH ARMY in September 1943.
_notes.Soviet Union: The Stalin Line's skeleton crews on 22 June 1941, about 0.2 a region. No Mogilev row: the record's 'Mogilev' region was Mogilev-Podolsky, in Vinnitsa's province; its 0.2 goes to Mozyr's region, Gomel on this chart. Minsk 0.3. No Kiev row: the city's garrison (city-garrisons-b605.md) already holds its region's skeleton.
_notes.Germany: No row for 1939-40: field divisions held the West Wall. In September 1944 it was manned by fortress machine-gun battalions and Landesschuetzen, leaning north where the Allies came first.
_notes.Greece: The forts' share of the Eastern Macedonia Army Section: 20 of 21 forts stood west of the Nestos.
_notes.None owed: The Mannerheim Line, the Grebbe Line, the Albert Canal, the Peel-Raam Line and the West Wall of 1939-40 were held by field divisions.

_stores: Each crew's own stores, in months, from the month the supply picture cuts it off (the design director's 06:41Z, on the historian's 06:50Z addendum to fortress-garrisons-by-line.md): each month cut off it eats one, counted apart from its organisation (the design director's 09:06Z): it holds its organisation and its strength while they last, and gives in the month they run out; a month fed in supply restocks it. A port fed by sea is not cut off. A computer staff round a crew-held town reads the same clock (siege.ts stormBar, the design director's 13:05Z), and so does the siege card, for both sides. null: no stores clock; the row yields only with its army. A row not named takes storesDefault, marked judgment. The historian's point: no works line yielded because its food ran out while its army still fought; stores are a ceiling, and holds ended by orders, the army's yield, assault, or shells and water.
_crewXp: A fortress crew's experience (the design director's 11:56Z of 22 November 2026, on the historian's fortress-storm-rows.md): trained, not green. The record's crews were full-time specialist cadres with reservists from the district, trained on their own works though untried in battle; every nation's fortress troops are read by that same test, the book's rows here and the first-day rows of setup-1939.json and far-world.json alike. 0.25 is the setup's own figure for a trained formation of 1939 (France's active 1st and 7th Armies; the card's word for 0.2 to 0.45 is trained). A crew that has more keeps it, and drafts into a crew come in at this figure, not the depots' green. Nothing is set for a storm: the attackers fight at whatever their own corps carry.

FRA:Metz fortified region.note: the Maginot's design intent: 'capable of resisting for three months, even if surrounded'

GRE:Metaxas Line forts.note: no stores clock: it yielded WITH ARMY (9-10 April 1941)
